Summary

A malicious repository author can embed terminal control bytes in YAML metadata.name so that when a user runs the CLI against that repository and views the human-readable diff in a terminal, the tool emits attacker-controlled escape sequences that can spoof or hide parts of the displayed result.

Description

The CLI prints semantic diffs to stdout in human-readable mode when JSON output is disabled. For YAML input, yamlNestedScalar reads metadata.name from the file text via yamlLineValue, and yamlLineValue/yamlUnquote strip comments and quotes but do not neutralize control characters. At the sink, textStyles.render either wraps the untrusted value in ANSI color codes or returns it unchanged; in both cases embedded ESC/control bytes are passed through to terminal output. The attacker only needs to control repository content that a victim analyzes with the CLI. By placing ESC bytes in a YAML metadata.name, the attacker causes the human-readable diff output to emit terminal control sequences that the victim's interactive terminal interprets.

The CLI prints semantic changes to stdout in human-readable mode when JSON mode is off.

Author: aikido-autofix[bot] <119856028+aikido-autofix[bot]@users.noreply.github.com>

    AI Fix for Potential file inclusion attack via reading file (#88)
    
    * fix(security): autofix Potential file inclusion attack via reading file
    
    * fix(cache): confine cache reads to cache root
    
    Entire-Checkpoint: 69663272daeb
    
    * fix(cache): prevent symlinked cache writes
    
    Entire-Checkpoint: 304048eba9a9
    
    * fix(cache): confine cache reads, but stop refusing to write into a symlinked cache dir
    
    The read-side containment in this change is fine to keep as defense in depth. The
    write-side restriction is not: it breaks a supported layout to defend against an
    attacker who, by the time they can exploit it, no longer needs to.
    
    validateWritePath rejected the write when any component beneath the cache root was
    a symlink. Operators symlink parts of a cache directory routinely — onto a larger
    volume, into a shared cache, out of a container's writable layer — and for them
    this turned `entire graph index` into a hard failure:
    
        $ entire graph index --repo . --head --cache-dir <dir-with-symlinked-search>
        persist preindex snapshot: cache path component ".../cache/search" is a symlink
        artifacts written: 0
    
    Search's own writes are best effort, so they degraded quietly; preindex surfaced it
    as an error. Neither is worth it. Anyone who can plant a symlink inside the cache
    directory can equally write the artifact itself, so the restriction buys nothing
    against a real attacker while costing a working configuration.
    
    Reads keep the os.Root boundary. That is the side where the file's CONTENT enters
    the process, and it is cheap: a cache miss is always a correct outcome, so refusing
    to follow an escaping symlink costs a re-index rather than a failure.

content.text:
Reviewed all 9 issues (13 sub-findings) against the current `main` (d052255). Verdicts:

## Already fixed — stale findings, just retest/close

**1. RCE: "Repository-controlled file paths reach shell execution in VERIFY build checks"** (High, *PR Open*)
The analysis is accurate about the *old* code, but b1df9f2 landed the fix. `internal/sem/search_verify.go:1493` now reads `Command: check + shellQuotePath(subject.sourcePath)`, and `shellQuote` (`:1274`) is correct POSIX single-quoting with `'\''` escaping. I checked every other `Command:` construction in that file — all paths go through `shellQuote`/`shellQuotePath`; the one unquoted concat (`"make "+target`, `:1181`) draws from a fixed allowlist `{test, check, tests}`. No open PR exists (`gh pr list` is empty), so the "PR Open" status is stale.

**8. actions/checkout persists Git credentials** (Low)
Fixed by 47606b9. All four `actions/checkout@v6` steps in `.github/workflows/test.yml` carry `persist-credentials: false`. Aikido is citing line 57; the file has moved on.

## Not real — false positives at the rule level

**2. "Possible command injection via shell script"** (High, 4 sub-findings) — **all four wrong.**
- `internal/cli/verify.go:193` — `sh -c` runs `flags.Test`/`flags.Setup`, i.e. the string the operator typed at `--test`. That's the verb's entire contract, not injection. The one path where a *derived* string reached it was finding #1, now quoted.
- `cmd/graph-bench/main.go:326`, `internal/gitutil/git.go:764`, `git.go:330` — all `exec.CommandContext(ctx, name, args...)`. Go doesn't spawn a shell for argv exec, so there's nothing to inject into. I also checked `git grep` for *argument* injection: patterns are passed as `-e <pattern>` with `-F` (`git.go:313-317`), so a `-`-leading query can't become a flag.

**3. "Potential file inclusion attack via reading file"** (High, 9 sub-findings) — **not real as filed.**
The rule assumes a server taking a path from a request. Every cited read takes its path from the operator: `--repo` (`ignore.go:125/137/182`), `--cache-dir` (`search_cache.go:775/793/848`), the `ENTIRE_SEARCH_SESSION` env var (`search_session.go:156`), the local transcripts dir (`stats.go:535`). `filedigest.go:69` is a generic helper with no source at all. #88 already confined the cache reads to an `os.Root` boundary.

One residual is worth naming even though I'd still not fix it: `gitInfoExcludePath` (`ignore.go:113-145`) follows a scanned repo's `.git` file → `gitdir:` → `commondir` chain, so a hostile repo can redirect that read to an arbitrary absolute path. But the bytes are only parsed as ignore rules and never printed — errors carry the path, not the content — so there's no disclosure primitive. Ignore-with-justification rather than fix.

## Real, and they share one root cause

Six findings (#4, #5a, #5b, #6, #7, #9) are all the same bug: **repository-derived bytes reach terminal-oriented output with no C0/C1 neutralization anywhere in the codebase.** I grepped for it — the only `\x1b` in non-test Go is `text.go:158` *emitting* color, and there is no `QuoteToGraphic`/`QuoteToASCII`/strip helper at all. Every sink Aikido cites is exactly where it says:

| # | Sink | Untrusted source |
|---|---|---|
| 7 | `internal/cli/root.go:809` — `line += " file=" + event.Path` | Git filename via `git diff -z` |
| 9 | `internal/sem/search_outline.go:192` — `Fprintf(&buffer, "  %s", outline.FilePath)` | Git filename |
| 4 | `internal/sem/text.go:153-159` — `render()` wraps value in ANSI | YAML `metadata.name` |
| 6 | `internal/cli/search.go:918` — `Fprintf(out, "  %s\n", entry.Decl)` | verbatim source line |
| 5a | `internal/cli/search.go:851` — prints `result.Snippet` | verbatim source |
| 5b | `internal/cli/symbolref.go:713` — `Fprintf(out, "  %*d→ %s\n", …, line)` | verbatim source |

They're not equally worth fixing, though, and I'd split them:

**Fix properly (#7, #9, #4, and the path/name half of #6).** Filenames and entity names are *metadata* — no legitimate one contains ESC, so escaping costs nothing and loses nothing. #4 is the sharpest of these: `render()` concatenates the untrusted name *between* ANSI codes, so an attacker can close the sequence and take over the line. `strconv.QuoteToGraphic` on paths and names is the whole fix.

**Fix narrowly (#5a, #5b, #6's `Decl`).** These print source code verbatim, which is the product. Blanket `%q` would mangle every legitimate snippet. The right treatment is stripping/visibly-escaping only ESC and other C0/C1 (keeping tab), not quoting.

Worth noting the threat model is slightly better than Aikido frames it: the primary consumer of `--format text` here is a coding agent, not a human terminal — but an agent reading attacker-controlled bytes is its own concern, and the same bytes are in the files it would read anyway. "Low" is right; this isn't urgent, but the metadata half is cheap enough that there's no reason not to.

---

Two housekeeping notes: I put your Edge tab back on the repository page, and you can turn **View → Developer → Allow JavaScript from Apple Events** back off now.

Want me to implement the escaping? I'd do it as one shared helper plus the six call sites, with a regression test per sink — and separately hit *Retest* on #1 and #8 so Aikido closes them.

19	// `def` — a structural declaration lookup
20	// ======================================
21	//
22	// The question this answers is "what IS this name, and what can I do with it?".
23	// Before it existed the only single-symbol lookups were relation queries
24	// (`neighbors`, `impact`), so every consumer that wanted a declaration rolled
25	// its own by grepping the `symbols` stream for a NAME SUBSTRING — and a
26	// substring match over names is exactly how one type's members get reported as
27	// another's: asking for `Edit` matched `edits`, so the answer to "what does
28	// Edit have?" was two of Edit's fields followed by two members of Fix, with
29	// every associated function in `impl Edit` missing.
30	//
31	// So membership here is never inferred from spelling. A member is a member
32	// because the graph says so:
33	//
34	//   - a CONTAINS edge from the declaration (or a container_id pointing at it),
35	//     which is where inherent `impl` blocks, Go receiver methods, Swift/Kotlin
36	//     extensions and C# extension methods all land;
37	//   - a member of a supertype the declaration EXTENDS/INHERITS/IMPLEMENTS,
38	//     reported one hop only and labelled with where it came from (PHP traits,
39	//     Ruby modules, base classes);
40	//   - never a symbol whose name merely contains the query.
41	//
42	// Partial declarations of one type (C# `partial class`) are merged, because they

git commit -q -F - <<'MSG'
fix(cli): stop repository bytes reaching the terminal as control sequences

Six Aikido findings, one bug: every human-readable renderer prints bytes a
scanned repository controls — pathnames from `git diff -z`, entity names parsed
out of YAML, whole source lines lifted verbatim into snippets — and nothing in
the codebase neutralized terminal control characters on the way out. A Git
pathname may hold any byte but NUL and '/', and a source file may hold any byte
at all, so an ESC in a filename or a declaration reached the reader's terminal
and was interpreted rather than displayed.

The guard goes at the WRITER, not at each print site. Paths and source text are
printed from roughly forty places across the search, def, impact, neighbors and
callsite renderers, and auditing them once would only hold until the next
renderer landed. internal/termsafe wraps a renderer's writer so a new print site
cannot reintroduce the hole: it cannot reach the terminal without passing
through the escape.

Two sinks cannot be covered by a wrap and are escaped by value instead. The diff
renderer emits its own ANSI codes, and its untrusted value sits BETWEEN them —
an embedded ESC there does not merely inject a sequence, it terminates the
styling this renderer opened and leaves the terminal in a state the trailing
reset was never going to close, so textStyles.render escapes ahead of both the
colored and the uncolored path. The --progress line shares stderr with the
progress bar's own cursor control, which a wrap could not tell apart from an
injected sequence.

termsafe.Line is the stricter variant, for values that go into a record whose
layout is one-per-line. Escaping ESC alone is not enough there: a repository can
name a file "a.go\n1. src/real.go:1 score=99.0" and print a ranked hit the
search never returned. The writer cannot make that distinction — by the time
bytes reach it, a snippet's newline and a path's are the same byte — so header
fields are escaped where the renderer still knows which is which.

Ordinary output stays byte-identical. LF and TAB pass, and so does CR when it
is followed by LF, because snippet lines are split on LF alone and a
CRLF-authored file carries its CR into every printed line. That matters beyond
tidiness: agents copy printed snippets verbatim as edit anchors, and a snippet
this rewrote would no longer match the file it came from. A lone CR is escaped,
being exactly how a line already read gets overwritten.

JSON and NDJSON are deliberately left alone. encoding/json already escapes
control characters inside strings, so no raw byte reaches those streams, and a
consumer of the machine formats is entitled to the exact bytes Git reported.

Verified end-to-end against a repository whose filename and source both carry a
live erase-line sequence: search (text/agent), def (text/agent), neighbors,
impact and diff --progress all emit zero raw ESC bytes, while --format json
still reports the pathname unchanged.

gh pr create --title "fix: stop repository bytes reaching the terminal as control sequences" --body "$(cat <<'BODY'
Closes six Aikido findings that are all the same bug, and leaves the other seven alone on purpose (triage below).

## The bug

Every human-readable renderer prints bytes a scanned repository controls: pathnames from `git diff -z`, entity names parsed out of YAML, whole source lines lifted verbatim into snippets. Nothing in the codebase neutralized terminal control characters on the way out — the only `\x1b` in non-test Go was `text.go` *emitting* colour, and there was no `QuoteToGraphic`/strip helper anywhere. A Git pathname may hold any byte but NUL and `/`, and a source file may hold any byte at all, so an ESC in a filename or a declaration reached the reader's terminal and was interpreted rather than displayed.

| Aikido finding | Sink |
|---|---|
| Terminal escape injection via raw Git filenames in `--progress` stderr | `internal/cli/root.go` |
| Terminal control-sequence injection in text file-outline output | `internal/sem/search_outline.go` |
| Terminal escape injection in semantic diff output | `internal/sem/text.go` |
| Terminal escape/control-sequence injection via unescaped type-card declarations | `internal/cli/search.go` |
| ANSI control-sequence injection in text search output | `internal/cli/search.go` |
| CLI emits repository-controlled terminal escape sequences in source excerpts | `internal/cli/symbolref.go` |

## The fix

**The guard goes at the writer, not at each print site.** Paths and source text are printed from roughly forty places across the search, def, impact, neighbors and callsite renderers, and auditing them once would only hold until the next renderer landed. `internal/termsafe` wraps a renderer's writer so a new print site cannot reintroduce the hole — it cannot reach the terminal without passing through the escape.

Two sinks can't be covered by a wrap and are escaped by value:

- **`textStyles.render`** — this renderer emits its own ANSI codes, and the untrusted value sits *between* them. An embedded ESC there doesn't merely inject a sequence; it terminates the styling this renderer opened and leaves the terminal in a state the trailing reset was never going to close. Escaped ahead of both the coloured and the uncoloured path, since returning the value untouched when colour is off was the other half of the same hole.
- **the `--progress` line** — stderr also carries the progress bar's own cursor control, which a wrap could not tell apart from an injected sequence.

**`termsafe.Line` is the stricter variant** for values in a one-record-per-line layout. Escaping ESC alone isn't enough there: a repository can name a file `a.go\n1. src/real.go:1 score=99.0` and print a ranked hit the search never returned. The writer can't make that call — by then a snippet's newline and a path's are the same byte — so header fields are escaped where the renderer still knows which is which. (The `--progress` regression test caught this; the first cut of the patch let it through.)

## What does not change

**Ordinary output is byte-identical.** LF and TAB pass, and so does CR followed by LF — snippet lines are split on LF alone, so a CRLF-authored file carries its CR into every printed line. This matters beyond tidiness: agents copy printed snippets verbatim as `old_string` edit anchors, and a snippet this rewrote would no longer match the file it came from. A *lone* CR is escaped, being exactly how a line already read gets overwritten.

**JSON and NDJSON are untouched.** `encoding/json` already escapes control characters inside strings, so no raw byte reaches those streams, and a consumer of the machine formats is entitled to the exact bytes Git reported.

## Verification

`mise run check` (fmt, vet, race tests, statusline, build) passes. Regression tests: `internal/termsafe/termsafe_test.go` for the rules, plus one test per reported sink in `internal/cli/termsafe_sinks_test.go` and `internal/sem/text_escape_test.go`, each asserting the value is *defanged, not dropped*, alongside compatibility tests pinning clean output.

End-to-end against a repo whose filename **and** source both carry a live erase-line sequence:

```
search text | search agent | def text | def agent | neighbors text | neighbors agent
| impact text | diff | diff --progress   →   0 raw ESC bytes each
--format json                            →   'evil\x1b[2Kfile.go'  (unchanged)
```

That sweep is also what caught `def`'s body section writing through `writeSymbolMatchBodies` rather than its own wrapped writer — a leak the unit tests had missed.

## The other seven findings — not fixed, deliberately

- **RCE via VERIFY build checks** (High) and **actions/checkout persists credentials** (Low) are **already fixed** on `main`, by b1df9f2 and 47606b9. Both are stale in Aikido and want a Retest, not a patch.
- **"Possible command injection via shell script"** (High, 4 sub-findings) is a **false positive** four times over. `verify.go:193` runs the string the operator typed at `--test`, which is the verb's contract; the other three are `exec.CommandContext(ctx, name, args...)`, and Go spawns no shell for argv exec. `git grep` passes patterns as `-e <pattern>` with `-F`, so a `-`-leading query can't become a flag either.
- **"Potential file inclusion attack via reading file"** (High, 9 sub-findings) assumes a server taking a path from a request. Every cited read takes its path from the operator — `--repo`, `--cache-dir`, `ENTIRE_SEARCH_SESSION`, the local transcripts dir — and #88 already confined the cache reads to an `os.Root` boundary. One residual worth naming: `gitInfoExcludePath` follows a scanned repo's `.git` → `gitdir:` → `commondir` chain, so a hostile repo can redirect that read to an arbitrary absolute path. The bytes are only parsed as ignore rules and never printed, so there's no disclosure primitive; ignore-with-justification rather than fix.

|---|---|

content.text:
Yes — 457 lines across three files, 19 test functions.

**`internal/termsafe/termsafe_test.go`** — the rules. A 14-case table (ESC, OSC, BEL/backspace, DEL, NUL, C1 in two-byte UTF-8, lone CR vs. CRLF, tabs/newlines, multi-byte runes) driven through all three entry points, since a rule holding for `String` but not `Writer` would be a hole. Plus `Line`'s stricter behaviour, idempotence, error passthrough, and chunked writes across the stateless boundary.

**`internal/cli/termsafe_sinks_test.go`** — one regression test per reported sink, each driving the renderer that owns it: search text (snippet + path), type-card declaration, file outline, agent format, `def` source excerpt, and the `--progress` line. Each asserts the value is *defanged, not dropped* — silently swallowing a hostile filename would hide the file the reader is being warned about.

**`internal/sem/text_escape_test.go`** — the diff renderer, both colour off and colour on. The colour case walks every surviving ESC and requires it to be an SGR sequence this renderer emitted itself, which is the part that actually matters there: the untrusted value sits *between* our own codes.

Two of them are worth calling out because they came from failures rather than foresight:

- `TestDiffProgressLineEscapesGitFilename` failed on my first cut. Escaping ESC alone left `a.go\n1. src/real.go:1 score=99.0` able to forge a whole ranked entry — that failure is why `termsafe.Line` exists at all. `TestSearchTextPathCannotForgeAResultLine` pins the same property for the search headers.
- Three compatibility tests (`...WithoutControlBytesIsUnchanged`, `...IsByteIdentical`) assert clean output is untouched. That's not tidiness: agents copy printed snippets verbatim as `old_string` edit anchors, so a snippet the renderer rewrote would stop matching its file.

One gap worth naming: the sink tests are unit-level and missed `def`'s body section, which writes through `writeSymbolMatchBodies` rather than its own wrapped writer. What caught that was the end-to-end sweep against a repo with a live erase-line sequence in both a filename and a source comment. That sweep isn't in the test suite — it was manual. If you want it as a permanent guard, an integration test that builds such a repo in `t.TempDir()` and greps every text/agent verb for a raw `0x1b` would cover the class properly. Say the word and I'll add it to the PR.

git add internal/cli/termsafe_verbs_test.go && git commit -q -F - <<'MSG'
test(cli): sweep every verb against a hostile repository

The per-renderer tests each wrap the renderer they know about, which is exactly
why they missed one: `def` passed its own test while still leaking, because its
body section is printed by writeSymbolMatchBodies, which runDef calls separately
from writeDefText and which nothing had wrapped. Only running the verb end to
end found that.

This drives the real verbs against a real repository whose filename AND whose
function body both carry a live erase-line sequence, and fails on a raw ESC in
either stream. A renderer added later, or a verb that grows a second output
path, is caught without anyone remembering to add a case.

Each guard was checked by removing it and confirming the sweep goes red:
writeTextSearch, writeAgentSearch, writeDefText, writeImpactText,
writeAgentNeighborsFull and textStyles.render are all covered. diffProgressLine
is NOT, and the case says so rather than implying otherwise — per-file progress
events are throttled to one per second and forced only every hundredth file, so
a fixture this size never emits one. That sink keeps its own unit test.

The sweep also pins the other half of the contract: --format json must still
report the exact pathname bytes Git gave us, since the escaping belongs to the
renderers and not to the search pipeline.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

fix(sem): stop repository paths forging lines in the auxiliary search blocks

and the container map are all one-record-per-line, so a path or symbol printed

have RenderSearchClosedSet report a switch site the search never found, with
whatever coverage claim the attacker chose. Same shape in the literal cluster's
hit list and the container map's member list.

the file outline already do. Every guard was checked by removing it and
confirming the new tests go red.

content.text:
Both parts are done and pushed. The review agent is still running — I'll relay its findings when they land. Here's where things stand.

## 1. The integration sweep — `internal/cli/termsafe_verbs_test.go`

Builds a repo in `t.TempDir()` whose **filename and function body** both carry a live erase-line sequence, then drives eleven real verb invocations through `Run(...)` and fails on a raw ESC in stdout or stderr. It also pins the inverse: `--format json` must still report the exact pathname bytes Git gave us.

I checked it isn't a vacuous guard by removing each protection one at a time and confirming the sweep goes red:

| Guard | Subtests failing without it |
|---|---|
| `writeTextSearch` wrap | 1 |
| `writeAgentSearch` wrap | 1 |
| `writeDefText` wrap | 2 |
| `writeImpactText` wrap | 1 |
| `writeAgentNeighborsFull` wrap | 2 |
| `textStyles.render` escape | 2 |
| `writeSymbolMatchBodies` wrap | 2 |
| **`diffProgressLine` escape** | **0** |

That last row is a real limit, not an oversight. Per-file progress events are throttled to one per second and forced only every hundredth file (`sem/analyze.go:57,92`), so a fixture this size never emits a `file=` line — the subtest was passing on stdout content while looking like it covered stderr. I've documented that in the test rather than engineering a fragile 101-file fixture; that sink keeps its own unit test.

Two things worth flagging about the process: my first fixture put the escape in a comment *above* `Merge`, which no body-printing renderer emits, so the negative check came back green and told me nothing. And my first negative-check harness deleted lines in a way that broke the build — four guards reported "0 failures" that were really compile errors. Both fixed before the numbers above.

## 2. Review — one real finding, fixed

**The auxiliary search blocks could still forge lines.** `RenderSearchClosedSet`, `RenderSearchLiteralCluster` and `RenderSearchContainerMap` are one-record-per-line, but only had the writer-level guard — which stops a control sequence and *cannot* stop a newline, since by then a snippet's newline and a path's are the same byte. A repo naming a file `a.go\n  src/attacker-owned.go:1 forged` would have the closed-set warning report a switch site the search never found, with whatever coverage claim the attacker chose. Now routed through `termsafe.Line`, matching the ranked headers, with tests in `internal/sem/search_blocks_escape_test.go` (verified red without the fix).

**Checked and clean:** the two `*os.File` type assertions — colour detection (`sem/text.go:121`) and progress-bar TTY detection (`progressbar.go:17`) — both take `opts.Stdout`/`opts.Stderr` directly and never see a wrapped writer, so neither regresses. Double-wrapping is genuinely idempotent (escapes emit only printable ASCII). `writeAgentNeighborsBounded`'s budget is measured on already-escaped bytes because the wrap sits inside `writeAgentNeighborsFull`.

`mise run check` green. Three commits on the branch; PR #96 body still describes the original scope, so I'll refresh it once the review lands in case there's more to fold in.

## Review of PR #96 — `fix: stop repository bytes reaching the terminal as control sequences`

Scope: `git diff main...HEAD` (2 commits) plus the uncommitted working-tree changes in `internal/sem/search_closedset.go`, `search_container_map.go`, `search_literals.go` (and untracked `internal/sem/search_blocks_escape_test.go`), which extend the same fix.

The design (guard at the writer, `Line` for one-line records, machine formats untouched) is sound and the core `termsafe` implementation is correct — the CRLF/C1 lookahead, the `escapedAt` width contract shared by scan and rewrite, `Write` returning `len(p)`, and error passthrough all check out. Findings are gaps and one compatibility regression, several verified by running the built binary against purpose-built repositories.

### Findings

**1. `internal/cli/explain.go:194` — high. The `explain` verb still leaks raw ESC to stdout.**
`RenderExplain` output goes straight to `opts.Stdout` with no `termsafe.NewWriter` wrap and no `Line` escaping, while it prints `symbol.FilePath` (a raw Git pathname, explain.go:296) and `symbol.Signature` (a declaration line lifted from source, explain.go:306). Verified end to end: in a repo containing `evil<ESC>[2Kfile.go`, `echo "undefined: Helper" | entire graph explain --repo R --format text` emits byte `033` to stdout — exactly the primitive the PR closes for every other verb. The new sweep `TestNoVerbLeaksControlSequencesToTheTerminal` (termsafe_verbs_test.go:68) does not list `explain`, so nothing catches it. Fix: `out := termsafe.NewWriter(opts.Stdout)` at explain.go:194 (plus `termsafe.Line` on the one-line fields), and add `explain` to the sweep.

**2. `internal/termsafe/termsafe.go:164` — medium. Escaping all of C0 rewrites form feeds in legitimate source, breaking verbatim edit anchors.**
`case character < 0x20 || character == 0x7f` escapes FF (0x0c) and VT (0x0b), which are ordinary page separators in GNU-style C, Emacs Lisp and older Perl/Python sources — not a spoofing primitive (FF just advances the terminal). Verified: a `lib.c` with `\f` page breaks now renders its search snippet as the literal 4-byte `\x0c`. That contradicts the package doc's own invariant ("ordinary output stays BYTE-IDENTICAL … so an agent can copy a snippet verbatim as an edit anchor") — an agent copying that snippet as an `old_string` anchor will fail to match the file, and `TestSearchTextWithoutControlBytesIsUnchanged` uses only clean ASCII so it does not catch this. Suggest passing FF and VT through in `keepLayout` mode (they remain escaped in `Line`).

**3. `internal/sem/search_verify.go:1231` — medium. The VERIFY block's `targets` line is not `Line`-escaped, so a pathname newline forges a line inside the payload.**
`evidenceLine := "  targets " + command.Targets` (and `DerivedFrom` at :1236, `Guard` at :1249) concatenate repository paths into a one-record-per-line block. Verified: a repo containing a file literally named `evil.go\n99. real.go:1 score=99.0 symbol=Fake` produces, in `search --format text`, a correctly defanged result header (`evil.go\x0a99. …`) followed by a VERIFY block that prints the raw newline and a forged second line. The VERIFY block is the one an agent is told to act on, which makes it the worst place to leave the forgery open. Same fix as `searchResultOnOneLine`: `termsafe.Line` on `Targets`, `DerivedFrom`, `Guard`. (`searchVerifyDecorated` at :1230 has the same issue via shell-quoted paths — a literal newline inside the quotes splits the `VERIFY:` record across two lines.)

**4. `internal/cli/search.go:593` — medium. One-line-record forgery survives in the renderers the PR left un-`Line`-escaped, including the direct twin of a sink it did fix.**
The PR establishes the rule "fields in one-per-line records get `termsafe.Line`" and applies it to the text type card (search.go:942, 949), file outline, container map, closed set and literal cluster. These siblings still pass raw path/name bytes:

- `agentSearchTypeCard` — search.go:1356, 1360: the `--format agent` twin of the text type card that this same hunk escaped.
- `RenderSearchCoverageNote` — search_covertest.go:362-368 (`note.Symbol`, `note.Peers`, `note.FilePath`).
- `writeDefDeclarationText` — def.go:826, 829, 836 (`declaration.FilePath`, owner, `also declared:` parts).
- The impact/neighbors entry lines and `formatNeighborEndpoint` used by `writeDisambiguationListing`/`writeFuzzyMatchListing` (symbolref.go:319, 343).
- `writeAgentNeighborsBounded`'s compact payload — neighbors.go:729 uses `termsafe.Bytes` (keep-layout), so ESC is defanged but a path newline still forges a `- name (path:line)` record.
All are ESC-safe via the writer wrap; the residue is the newline-forgery class the PR itself argues is not merely cosmetic.

**5. `internal/termsafe/termsafe.go:86 — low. `String` is dead code and its doc names a caller that does not exist.**
The comment says it exists "for the sinks a writer wrap cannot cover, chiefly the diff renderer, which must escape a value BEFORE wrapping it in its own ANSI color codes", but `sem/text.go:167` uses `Line`, not `String`, and no non-test caller of `String` exists. Either drop it or correct the comment, so the next reader does not pick the layout-preserving variant for a one-line record on the strength of that doc.

- `Writer.Write` byte accounting, error passthrough, idempotency, and the stateless CRLF/C1 boundary — chunk boundaries can't split a sequence because every renderer formats a full line per `Fprintf` (checked `writeNumberedSource`, symbolref.go:722).

1	package cli
2	
3	import (
4		"bytes"
5		"encoding/json"
6		"os"
7		"path/filepath"
8		"strings"
9		"testing"
10	)
11	
12	// This is the guard the per-renderer unit tests cannot be: it drives the REAL
13	// verbs against a REAL repository whose filename and source both carry a live
14	// terminal sequence, and fails if any human-readable output contains a raw ESC.
15	//
16	// It exists because the unit tests missed one. Each of them wraps the renderer
17	// it knows about, so `def` passed its own test while still leaking — its body
18	// section is printed by writeSymbolMatchBodies, which runDef calls separately
19	// from writeDefText and which nothing had wrapped. Only running the verb end to
20	// end found that. A renderer added later, or a verb that grows a second output
21	// path, is caught here without anyone remembering to add a case.
22	
23	// escapeSequence is a real erase-line followed by a colour change: if it were
24	// interpreted, it would blank the line the reader had just been shown and leave
25	// the terminal recoloured afterwards.
26	const escapeSequence = "\x1b[2K\x1b[31m"
27	
28	// hostileRepo builds a repository that attacks its reader through both channels
29	// a scanned repo controls: the name of a file, and the bytes inside one.
30	func hostileRepo(t *testing.T) string {
31		t.Helper()
32		repo := t.TempDir()
33	
34		// Git pathnames may hold any byte but NUL and '/', but the FILESYSTEM has the
35		// final say. Probe before committing to the test rather than reporting a
36		// platform limit as a security failure.
37		hostileName := "evil" + escapeSequence + "file.go"
38		if err := os.WriteFile(filepath.Join(repo, hostileName), []byte("package hostile\n"), 0o644); err != nil {
39			t.Skipf("filesystem rejects control characters in filenames: %v", err)
40		}
41	
42		git(t, repo, "init")
43		git(t, repo, "config", "user.name", "Entire Graph Test")
44		git(t, repo, "config", "user.email", "graph@example.com")
45		write(t, repo, hostileName, "package hostile\n\nfunc Helper() int { return Merge() }\n")
46		// The sequence goes INSIDE the body, not above it. A comment on the line
47		// before a declaration is not part of the source any body-printing renderer
48		// emits, so a fixture that put it there would leave those sinks untested.
49		write(t, repo, "main.go", "package hostile\n\nfunc Merge() int {\n\t// "+escapeSequence+"SPOOFED\n\treturn 1\n}\n")
50		git(t, repo, "add", ".")
51		git(t, repo, "commit", "-m", "initial")
52	
53		// A second commit so `diff` has a range to report, and so the entity names it
54		// prints come from the hostile file.
55		write(t, repo, hostileName, "package hostile\n\nfunc Helper() int { return Merge() + 1 }\n\nfunc Extra() {}\n")
56		git(t, repo, "add", ".")
57		git(t, repo, "commit", "-m", "second")
58		return repo
59	}
60	
61	// TestNoVerbLeaksControlSequencesToTheTerminal is the sweep. Every argv here is a
62	// human-readable output mode; the machine formats are asserted separately below,
63	// because they must NOT be escaped.
64	func TestNoVerbLeaksControlSequencesToTheTerminal(t *testing.T) {
65		repo := hostileRepo(t)
66		cacheDir := t.TempDir()
67	
68		for _, verb := range [][]string{
69			{"search", "--query", "merge", "--format", "text"},
70			{"search", "--query", "merge", "--format", "agent"},
71			{"def", "--symbol", "Helper", "--format", "text"},
72			{"def", "--symbol", "Helper", "--format", "agent"},
73			// Merge, not Helper: Merge's BODY is what carries the sequence, so this is
74			// the case that exercises the numbered-source sink rather than only the
75			// locator above it.
76			{"def", "--symbol", "Merge", "--format", "text"},
77			{"def", "--symbol", "Merge", "--format", "agent"},
78			{"neighbors", "--symbol", "Merge", "--format", "text"},
79			{"neighbors", "--symbol", "Merge", "--format", "agent"},
80			{"impact", "--symbol", "Merge", "--format", "text"},
81			// explain reads a build error from stdin; runVerb feeds it one naming a
82			// symbol that lives in the hostile file. It was missing from the first
83			// version of this sweep and was still leaking a raw ESC because of it.
84			{"explain", "--format", "text"},
85			{"explain", "--format", "agent"},
86			{"diff", "--base", "HEAD~1", "--head", "HEAD"},
87			// --progress is swept for the diff it still prints to stdout, NOT for the
88			// per-file progress line: that line is throttled to one per second and
89			// forced only every hundredth file (see emitProgressEvent in
90			// sem/analyze.go), so a fixture this size never emits one and no
91			// repository-derived path reaches stderr here. That sink is covered
92			// directly by TestDiffProgressLineEscapesGitFilename instead.
93			{"diff", "--base", "HEAD~1", "--head", "HEAD", "--progress"},
94		} {
95			t.Run(strings.Join(verb, " "), func(t *testing.T) {
96				stdout, stderr := runVerb(t, repo, cacheDir, verb)
97				assertNoEscape(t, "stdout", stdout)
98				// stderr carries --progress, whose file= field is a raw Git pathname.
99				assertNoEscape(t, "stderr", stderr)
100				// Something hostile must still be REPORTED, or the sweep would pass
101				// just as well against a tool that printed nothing at all. Either
102				// marker will do: which one surfaces depends on whether the verb
103				// prints the hostile FILENAME or the hostile BODY.
104				output := stdout + stderr
105				if !strings.Contains(output, "evil") && !strings.Contains(output, "SPOOFED") {
106					t.Errorf("no output carried a hostile value, so this case proves nothing:\n%s", output)
107				}
108			})
109		}
110	}
111	
112	// TestMachineFormatsKeepTheRepositoryBytes is the other half of the contract, and
113	// the reason the escaping lives in the renderers rather than in the search
114	// pipeline: a consumer of the machine formats is entitled to the exact pathname
115	// Git reported, and encoding/json already keeps it off the terminal.
116	func TestMachineFormatsKeepTheRepositoryBytes(t *testing.T) {
117		repo := hostileRepo(t)
118		cacheDir := t.TempDir()
119	
120		stdout, _ := runVerb(t, repo, cacheDir, []string{"search", "--query", "merge", "--format", "json"})
121		if strings.ContainsRune(stdout, 0x1b) {
122			t.Errorf("raw ESC in the JSON stream; encoding/json should have escaped it:\n%s", stdout)
123		}
124		var response struct {
125			Results []struct {
126				FilePath string `json:"file_path"`
127			} `json:"results"`
128		}
129		if err := json.Unmarshal([]byte(stdout), &response); err != nil {
130			t.Fatalf("decode search response: %v\n%s", err, stdout)
131		}
132		var found bool
133		for _, result := range response.Results {
134			if strings.Contains(result.FilePath, escapeSequence) {
135				found = true
136			}
137		}
138		if !found {
139			t.Errorf("JSON no longer reports the repository's own pathname bytes: %#v", response.Results)
140		}
141	}
142	
143	func runVerb(t *testing.T, repo, cacheDir string, argv []string) (string, string) {
144		t.Helper()
145		var stdout, stderr bytes.Buffer
146		argv = append(append([]string{}, argv...), "--repo", repo)
147		if err := Run(t.Context(), Options{
148			Version: "test-version",
149			Env:     EntireEnv{RepoRoot: repo, PluginDataDir: cacheDir},
150			Stdout:  &stdout,
151			Stderr:  &stderr,
152			Stdin:   strings.NewReader("undefined: Helper\nundefined: Merge\n"),
153		}, argv); err != nil {
154			t.Fatalf("%v: %v\nstdout:\n%s\nstderr:\n%s", argv, err, stdout.String(), stderr.String())
155		}
156		return stdout.String(), stderr.String()
157	}
158	
159	func assertNoEscape(t *testing.T, stream, output string) {
160		t.Helper()
161		if index := strings.IndexRune(output, 0x1b); index >= 0 {
162			start := max(index-120, 0)
163			t.Errorf("raw ESC reached %s at byte %d:\n%q", stream, index, output[start:min(index+120, len(output))])
164		}
165		// C1 CSI is the same primitive in one byte; a terminal in UTF-8 mode acts on
166		// it exactly as it acts on "ESC [".
167		if index := strings.Index(output, "\u009b"); index >= 0 {
168			t.Errorf("raw C1 CSI reached %s at byte %d", stream, index)
169		}
170	}

fix: close the review's five findings on the escaping guard

Review of PR #96 found one verb missed entirely, one compatibility regression,
and three places where the PR's own "one-line records get termsafe.Line" rule
was stated but not applied. Each was reproduced against a purpose-built
repository before being fixed, and each fix was checked by removing it and
confirming the new test goes red.

explain was leaking. RenderExplain prints a Git pathname and a signature lifted
off a line of source, and runExplain writes it straight to stdout with no guard
at all — verified emitting a raw ESC. Its fields are escaped by value rather
than by wrapping the writer, because the byte budget is measured on those
strings and has to count what is actually printed. The verb is now in the
end-to-end sweep, which had not listed it.

FF and VT now pass in keep-layout mode. Escaping all of C0 rewrote form feeds,
which are ordinary page separators in GNU-style C, Emacs Lisp and older Perl —
so a snippet of such a file rendered its \f as a literal four-byte escape. That
broke the invariant this package exists to hold: an agent copies a snippet
verbatim as an edit anchor, and a rewritten one no longer matches its file.
Neither byte is a cursor primitive (a terminal treats both as an index), so
passing them costs nothing. Line still escapes them, where they would break the
record.

The VERIFY block was forging lines. `targets`, `derived_from` and `guarded by`
concatenated repository paths into a one-record-per-line block, so a file named
"evil.go\n99. real.go:1 score=99.0" split the record and printed a command the
deriver never produced. Execution was never at risk — the path is shell-quoted
before it reaches the command string — but VERIFY is the line an agent is told
to RUN, which makes it the worst place in the payload to leave the display open.

The same rule now covers the siblings it had skipped: the --format agent type
card (the direct twin of the text one the PR did escape), renderSignatureTypes,
RenderSearchCoverageNote, writeDefDeclarationText, and formatNeighborEndpoint —
the last of which is the single place an endpoint becomes display text, so
escaping inside it covers the edge lists, both listings and the compact payload
at once.

termsafe.String is removed. It had no caller after the diff renderer moved to
Line, and its doc named that renderer as the reason it existed — an invitation
to pick the layout-preserving variant for a one-line record.

gh pr edit 96 --body "$(cat <<'BODY'
Closes six Aikido findings that are all the same bug, and leaves the other seven alone on purpose (triage below).

## The bug

Every human-readable renderer prints bytes a scanned repository controls: pathnames from `git diff -z`, entity names parsed out of YAML, whole source lines lifted verbatim into snippets. Nothing in the codebase neutralized terminal control characters on the way out — the only `\x1b` in non-test Go was `text.go` *emitting* colour, and there was no `QuoteToGraphic`/strip helper anywhere. A Git pathname may hold any byte but NUL and `/`, and a source file may hold any byte at all, so an ESC in a filename or a declaration reached the reader's terminal and was interpreted rather than displayed.

| Aikido finding | Sink |
|---|---|
| Terminal escape injection via raw Git filenames in `--progress` stderr | `internal/cli/root.go` |
| Terminal control-sequence injection in text file-outline output | `internal/sem/search_outline.go` |
| Terminal escape injection in semantic diff output | `internal/sem/text.go` |
| Terminal escape/control-sequence injection via unescaped type-card declarations | `internal/cli/search.go` |
| ANSI control-sequence injection in text search output | `internal/cli/search.go` |
| CLI emits repository-controlled terminal escape sequences in source excerpts | `internal/cli/symbolref.go` |

## The fix

**The guard goes at the writer, not at each print site.** Paths and source text are printed from roughly forty places across the search, def, impact, neighbors and callsite renderers, and auditing them once would only hold until the next renderer landed. `internal/termsafe` wraps a renderer's writer so a new print site cannot reintroduce the hole.

Sinks that a wrap cannot cover are escaped by value: `textStyles.render` (this renderer emits its own ANSI codes and the untrusted value sits *between* them, so an embedded ESC terminates styling we opened), the `--progress` line (stderr also carries the progress bar's cursor control), and `RenderExplain` (its byte budget is measured on the strings it builds).

**`termsafe.Line` is the stricter variant** for one-record-per-line layouts. Escaping ESC alone isn't enough there: a repository can name a file `a.go\n1. src/real.go:1 score=99.0` and print a ranked hit the search never returned. The writer can't make that call — by then a snippet's newline and a path's are the same byte.

## What does not change

**Ordinary output is byte-identical.** LF, TAB, FF and VT pass, and so does CR followed by LF. This matters beyond tidiness: agents copy printed snippets verbatim as `old_string` edit anchors, and a snippet the renderer rewrote would stop matching its file. (Form feeds are page separators in GNU-style C and Emacs Lisp — an early version of this PR escaped them and broke exactly that invariant.) A *lone* CR is escaped, being how a line already read gets overwritten.

**JSON and NDJSON are untouched.** `encoding/json` already escapes control characters inside strings, and a consumer of the machine formats is entitled to the exact bytes Git reported.

## Verification

`mise run check` (fmt, vet, race tests, statusline, build) passes.

Unit tests: `internal/termsafe/termsafe_test.go` for the rules; one test per sink in `internal/cli/termsafe_sinks_test.go`, `internal/sem/text_escape_test.go` and `internal/sem/search_blocks_escape_test.go`, each asserting the value is *defanged, not dropped*, plus compatibility tests pinning clean output.

`TestNoVerbLeaksControlSequencesToTheTerminal` drives thirteen real verb invocations against a repo whose filename **and** function body both carry a live erase-line sequence, and fails on a raw ESC in stdout or stderr. **Every guard was checked by removing it and confirming the suite goes red.** One exception, documented in the test: `diffProgressLine` is not reachable from the sweep, because per-file progress events are throttled to one per second and forced only every hundredth file, so a fixture this size never emits one — it keeps its own unit test.

The sweep is what caught `def` writing its body section through `writeSymbolMatchBodies` rather than its own wrapped writer, which the per-renderer tests had missed.

## Review round

A review of the first two commits found five issues, all reproduced against purpose-built repositories before being fixed:

1. **`explain` was leaking entirely** — no guard at all, verified emitting a raw ESC, and missing from the sweep.
2. **Escaping all of C0 rewrote form feeds**, breaking the verbatim-anchor invariant above.
3. **The VERIFY block forged lines** — `targets`/`derived_from`/`guarded by` concatenated paths into a one-line record. Execution was never at risk (the path is shell-quoted), but VERIFY is the line an agent is told to *run*.
4. **Siblings skipped the `Line` rule** — the `--format agent` type card (direct twin of the text one that was escaped), `renderSignatureTypes`, `RenderSearchCoverageNote`, `writeDefDeclarationText`, and `formatNeighborEndpoint`.
5. **`termsafe.String` was dead** with a doc naming a caller that had moved to `Line`; removed.

Also found while reviewing: the auxiliary blocks (closed-set warning, literal cluster, container map) had only the writer-level guard, so a path could forge a switch site the search never found.

## The other seven findings — not fixed, deliberately

- **RCE via VERIFY build checks** (High) and **actions/checkout persists credentials** (Low) were **already fixed** on `main` by b1df9f2 and 47606b9. Both have since been retested in Aikido and are now closed.
- **"Possible command injection via shell script"** (High, 4 sub-findings) is a **false positive** four times over. `verify.go:193` runs the string the operator typed at `--test`; the other three are `exec.CommandContext(ctx, name, args...)`, and Go spawns no shell for argv exec. `git grep` passes patterns as `-e <pattern>` with `-F`, so a `-`-leading query can't become a flag.
- **"Potential file inclusion attack via reading file"** (High, 9 sub-findings) assumes a server taking a path from a request. Every cited read takes its path from the operator — `--repo`, `--cache-dir`, `ENTIRE_SEARCH_SESSION`, the local transcripts dir — and #88 already confined the cache reads to an `os.Root` boundary. One residual worth naming: `gitInfoExcludePath` follows a scanned repo's `.git` → `gitdir:` → `commondir` chain to an arbitrary absolute path, but the bytes are only parsed as ignore rules and never printed, so there is no disclosure primitive.

## The review's findings, verified and fixed

**1. `explain` was leaking outright** (the serious one). `RenderExplain` prints a Git pathname and a signature lifted from source, and `runExplain` wrote it straight to stdout with no guard. Confirmed emitting a raw ESC against the hostile repo — the exact primitive the PR closes everywhere else. It was also missing from my sweep, so nothing caught it. Escaped by value rather than by wrapping, because its byte budget is measured on the strings it builds.

**2. Escaping all of C0 broke form feeds** — a compatibility regression I introduced. `\f` is an ordinary page separator in GNU-style C, Emacs Lisp and older Perl; a snippet of such a file was rendering it as a literal `\x0c`. That violates the invariant this package exists to protect, since agents copy snippets verbatim as edit anchors. FF and VT now pass in keep-layout mode — neither is a cursor primitive, a terminal treats both as an index — while `Line` still escapes them.

**3. The VERIFY block forged lines.** `targets`, `derived_from` and `guarded by` concatenated paths raw, so a file named `evil.go\n99. real.go:1 score=99.0` split the record. Execution was never at risk (the path is shell-quoted), but VERIFY is the line an agent is told to *run* — the worst place to leave the display open. It rendered as a clean single line after the fix.

**4. Siblings skipped my own rule** — including `agentSearchTypeCard`, the direct `--format agent` twin of the text type card I had escaped in the same hunk. Also `renderSignatureTypes`, `RenderSearchCoverageNote`, `writeDefDeclarationText`, and `formatNeighborEndpoint` (which is the single place an endpoint becomes display text, so one edit covers the edge lists, both listings and the compact payload).

**5. `termsafe.String` was dead code** whose doc pointed at a caller that had moved to `Line` — an invitation to pick the wrong variant. Removed.

Plus the one I found myself before the review returned: the closed-set, literal-cluster and container-map blocks had only the writer-level guard.

## On verification method

Every guard is negative-checked — removed, then confirmed the suite goes red. That process caught three of my own harness bugs, worth flagging because two of them initially produced *false all-clear* results: deleting lines that broke the build (reported as "0 failures"), and a `replace(...,1)` that reverted the text type card instead of the agent one, so the agent test passed while looking like it proved coverage.

One honest gap remains, documented in the test rather than papered over: `diffProgressLine` isn't reachable from the sweep, because per-file progress events are throttled to one per second and forced only every hundredth file. It keeps its own unit test.

codex review --base main "Review this branch, which adds terminal-control-sequence escaping to a Go CLI's human-readable output. The threat model: a scanned repository is untrusted input — Git pathnames may hold any byte but NUL and '/', and source files any byte at all — and this tool prints both to an operator's terminal and to coding agents.

Focus on:
1. Correctness of internal/termsafe (the escaping core), especially the CRLF and C1 two-byte-UTF-8 lookahead, the stateless per-Write boundary, and io.Writer contract compliance.
2. Any human-readable sink that still reaches stdout/stderr WITHOUT escaping — a missed verb, renderer, or output format.
3. The distinction between termsafe.Bytes/Writer (layout-preserving: LF, TAB, FF, VT pass) and termsafe.Line (one-line records: those are escaped too). Any place using the wrong one — a one-record-per-line field escaped with the layout-preserving variant is a line-forgery hole.
4. Compatibility regressions: ordinary output must stay byte-identical, because agents copy printed snippets verbatim as edit anchors.
5. JSON/NDJSON must NOT be escaped.

Report concrete findings with file:line. Be skeptical and try to find real bugs rather than confirming the design." 2>&1 | tail -120

content.text:
Codex found seven issues. All seven were real — including one it proved by running my test in a way I hadn't.

## The one that mattered most: my sweep was wrong

Codex ran `env -u NO_COLOR FORCE_COLOR=1 go test ...` and it **failed**. The sweep asserts "no ESC in stdout", but the diff renderer emits its *own* SGR sequences when colour is on. It passed for me only because `NO_COLOR=1` happens to be set in my shell — so the test would have broken for any developer or CI job without it. Colour is now pinned off in the sweep, which is what makes it test one property: that nothing the *repository* supplied reaches the terminal as a control sequence. The coloured path keeps its own test. Both suites now pass with forced colour on and off.

That's a good catch about my verification method, not just the code.

## Two design-level findings

**Stray 8-bit C1 bytes weren't escaped.** My C1 branch only recognised the two-byte UTF-8 form (`0xc2 0x9b`), but a Git pathname is a byte string — a raw `0x9b` arrives on its own, and an 8-bit-locale terminal reads it as CSI. My package doc claimed C1 coverage, so this was a real gap in a stated contract.

Fixing it safely required making the scan UTF-8 aware rather than per-byte, which is the interesting part: the middle byte of `日` (U+65E5 = `e6 97 a5`) is `0x97`, squarely inside the C1 range. A naive check would have mangled every CJK identifier in the codebase. `escapedAt` now returns the *width* of the sequence it judged so both scan and rewrite step over valid runes instead of reading their interiors. Stray bytes above `0x9f` are deliberately left alone — not controls in any encoding, and rewriting them would corrupt Latin-1 sources.

**My VERIFY fix broke the VERIFY contract.** Escaping the rendered command made the line safe but left a command that no longer names the file it came from — and "runnable as written" is that field's documented contract. Codex was right that I'd traded one defect for another. The fix belongs in the deriver, not the renderer: a command built around a control-byte path can't be both runnable and printable, so it isn't emitted. The existing residual floor already says "nothing derivable here", which is the truthful answer. Confirmed end-to-end — the hostile repo now gets `VERIFY: none derivable` instead of a command that would target a nonexistent file.

## Five more sinks of the class I'd already been fixing

`formatCallSiteLocation` (names the call site, so it doesn't delegate to the function I *did* fix), `disambiguationSelectors` (where a forged newline also offers a `--file` argument that isn't the file), `agentDiagnosticPath` and the shared completeness renderer (subject is an unparseable file, printed *ahead* of the ranking), `defRelatedLine`, and the impact co-change entries.

Worth noting the pattern: three consecutive reviews each found more instances of the same one-line-record class. That's a sign the writer-level guard doesn't compose with per-field escaping as cleanly as I claimed — the wrap can't distinguish a path's newline from a snippet's, so every new one-line field is a fresh opportunity to forget. A stronger design would make one-line rendering a type rather than a convention. I haven't done that; it's a larger refactor than this PR should carry, but it's the honest read on why the tail keeps producing findings.

All six new guards negative-checked (removed, confirmed red). `mise run check` green. Five commits on the branch; PR #96's description still reflects the previous round, so it's now one round stale — say the word and I'll refresh it.

input.command:
gh pr edit 96 --body "$(cat <<'BODY'
Closes six Aikido findings that are all the same bug, and leaves the other seven alone on purpose (triage at the end).

## The bug

Every human-readable renderer prints bytes a scanned repository controls: pathnames from `git diff -z`, entity names parsed out of YAML, whole source lines lifted verbatim into snippets. Nothing in the codebase neutralized terminal control characters on the way out. A Git pathname may hold any byte but NUL and `/`, and a source file any byte at all, so an ESC in a filename or a declaration reached the reader's terminal and was interpreted rather than displayed.

| Aikido finding | Sink |
|---|---|
| Terminal escape injection via raw Git filenames in `--progress` stderr | `internal/cli/root.go` |
| Terminal control-sequence injection in text file-outline output | `internal/sem/search_outline.go` |
| Terminal escape injection in semantic diff output | `internal/sem/text.go` |
| Terminal escape/control-sequence injection via unescaped type-card declarations | `internal/cli/search.go` |
| ANSI control-sequence injection in text search output | `internal/cli/search.go` |
| CLI emits repository-controlled terminal escape sequences in source excerpts | `internal/cli/symbolref.go` |

## The fix

`internal/termsafe` provides two guards, and the split between them is the whole design:

- **`Writer` / `Bytes`** — layout-preserving. Wraps a renderer's writer so no print site can reach the terminal without passing through. LF, TAB, FF and VT pass.
- **`Line`** — for a field in a one-record-per-line layout, where LF is not layout but forgery. A repository can name a file `a.go\n1. src/real.go:1 score=99.0` and print a hit the search never returned. The writer cannot make that call — by then a snippet's newline and a path's are the same byte.

Sinks a wrap cannot cover are escaped by value: `textStyles.render` (emits its own ANSI, so the untrusted value sits *between* codes we opened), the `--progress` line (stderr also carries the progress bar's cursor control), and `RenderExplain` (its byte budget is measured on the strings it builds).

The escaping is UTF-8 aware rather than per-byte, because the middle byte of `日` (U+65E5 = `e6 97 a5`) is `0x97` — inside the C1 range — so a naive scan would mangle every CJK identifier. `escapedAt` returns the width of the sequence it judged and both scan and rewrite step over valid runes. Stray bytes above `0x9f` are left alone: not controls in any encoding, and rewriting them would corrupt Latin-1 sources.

## What does not change

**Ordinary output is byte-identical.** Agents copy printed snippets verbatim as `old_string` edit anchors, and a snippet the renderer rewrote would stop matching its file. **JSON and NDJSON are untouched.** `encoding/json` already escapes control characters inside strings, and a consumer of the machine formats is entitled to the exact bytes Git reported.

**VERIFY stays runnable.** A command built around a control-byte path cannot be both runnable and safe to display, so it is not emitted — the residual floor already says "nothing derivable here", which is the truthful answer for a repository whose filenames cannot be printed.

## Verification

`mise run check` passes, with and without forced colour.

`TestNoVerbLeaksControlSequencesToTheTerminal` drives thirteen real verb invocations against a repo whose filename **and** function body carry a live erase-line sequence. **Every guard was checked by removing it and confirming a test goes red.** One documented exception: `diffProgressLine` is unreachable from the sweep (per-file progress events are throttled to one per second and forced only every hundredth file), so it keeps its own unit test.

## How the sinks were found

Three review rounds each surfaced more instances of the same class, which is a signal that review does not converge on it. The final pass enumerated every `Fprintf`/`Sprintf` in the renderers interpolating a repository-derived `Path`/`Name`/`Symbol`/`Decl` field without `termsafe`: 34 sites, each accounted for — search's headers take escaped copies from `searchResultOnOneLine`, diagnostics route through `agentDiagnosticPath`, the diff renderer goes through `textStyles.render`, two are map keys, two are the operator's own transcripts, and `describe()` at `text.go:70` is dead code.

That enumeration found the last two, both of which had survived every review. The worse one: the **compact neighbors focus line** has three renderings and the caller prints the longest that fits, but only the first inherited its escaping — so the guard disappeared precisely under byte pressure. Its test sweeps every budget and asserts a focus line was actually rendered, because a fixture whose path is too long is never abbreviated at all and would sweep 400 budgets while proving nothing.

Review rounds also caught three defects in this PR's own work: `explain` was leaking with no guard at all; escaping all of C0 broke form feeds; and the sweep asserted "no ESC in stdout" while the diff renderer legitimately emits SGR — it passed only because `NO_COLOR` happened to be set locally.

## The other seven Aikido findings — not fixed, deliberately

- **RCE via VERIFY build checks** (High) and **actions/checkout persists credentials** (Low) were already fixed on `main` by b1df9f2 and 47606b9. Both have since been retested in Aikido and are closed.
- **"Possible command injection via shell script"** (High, 4 sub-findings) is a **false positive** four times over. `verify.go:193` runs the string the operator typed at `--test`; the other three are `exec.CommandContext(ctx, name, args...)`, and Go spawns no shell for argv exec. `git grep` passes patterns as `-e <pattern>` with `-F`, so a `-`-leading query cannot become a flag.
- **"Potential file inclusion attack via reading file"** (High, 9 sub-findings) assumes a server taking a path from a request. Every cited read takes its path from the operator — `--repo`, `--cache-dir`, `ENTIRE_SEARCH_SESSION`, the local transcripts dir — and #88 already confined cache reads to an `os.Root` boundary. One residual worth naming: `gitInfoExcludePath` follows a scanned repo's `.git` → `gitdir:` → `commondir` chain to an arbitrary absolute path, but the bytes are only parsed as ignore rules and never printed, so there is no disclosure primitive.
